subject: shotgun
label: shotgun, in the place of the game's models/v_shotgun.mdl, models/p_shotgun.mdl, models/w_shotgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_egon.mdl, models/w_gauss.mdl, models/w_9mmar.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, A, B where the asset was C, B, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a straight red rod about 31.6 units long with a grey hook at one end (sides.png, FRONT, TOP and BELOW views). It has no receiver, pump, trigger guard, barrel or folding stock, so it does not have a pump shotgun's silhouette in any of the six views.

M2.reason: Length is 31.6 against the 30 the brief asks for, about 5% over and well within 15% (measured sizeOff 0.054). The brief gives only a length, so width (1.3) and height (5.7) are not held to a size.

M3.reason: The brief names a pump, a folding stock whose end hooks over, a black metal body and a wooden or dark pump. Only the hook is present, as the grey end of the rod. The pump, receiver, trigger and guard, and folding stock are all missing.

M4.reason: The shaft is glossy red and the hook is light grey (lineup.png A, sides.png). The brief asks for black metal and a wooden or dark pump. There is no black metal and no wood or dark pump region anywhere.

M5.reason: The surface is flat shading with no receiver edges, panel lines, grooves or wear, so it reads as a plain rod rather than a gun's metal. The brief names no marking, but this is clearly off for a black metal combat shotgun.

M6.reason: Scored below the instructed 2 on purpose, since the rule is that a judge may score lower than the measurement allows, never higher. The line-up measure itself caps this at 1: the asset was picked as the non-Valve model 2 of 4 times (picks C, C, A, B against asset positions C, B, A, C), and picked twice or more caps M6 at 1. The picture also shows a red crowbar, not a shotgun, which a player would not take for one of the game's. This is a decoy and must fail.

M7.reason: The long axis runs along the length, and the rod stands upright in the sides views with its hook at the top. There is no muzzle or stock end to show which way the front faces, and the front view shows only a small end-on profile.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The asset has 94 triangles, under the median of 138 for Half-Life's own weapons of this kind and under three quarters of them (187). The ends are closed in the sides and attack frames, and nothing is open, inside out or floating.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the rod runs up and to the left from the hand area, held the way a crowbar is held. The shotgun's grip, its muzzle forward and its pump hand are absent, so the held pose does not match the game's shotgun. In attack.png the swing carries the rod out of the picture, which does not count as leaving the hands. The pose is wrong, not the attachment.
